analysis.investment_thesis: A small-cap defense supplier growing revenue at 46% CAGR but trading at 73x earnings with negative free cash flow in 3 of the last 4 years — accounting profits are not translating into owner earnings. At 10.9x book and a ₹1,516 Cr cap on just ₹24 Cr of net profit, there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Strong top-line growth: Revenue 47→146 Cr (45.8% 3Y CAGR), net profit 8→24 Cr
Decent ROCE of 23.65% and moderate ROE of 16.13%
Promoter holding high at 68.06% and debt reduced from 46 to 21 Cr
key_risks: P/E 73 and P/B 10.9 — extreme valuation for a ₹24 Cr profit base
FCF negative three straight years (-29, -43, -8 Cr); profits not converting to cash
Cash collapsed from 17 Cr to 3 Cr in 2025 while capex continues — working-capital hungry
red_flags: Operating cash flow negative in 2023, 2024, 2025 despite rising reported earnings
Equity jumped 25→126 Cr in 2024 (financing CF +59 Cr) — dilution-funded growth, not self-funded
Negligible institutional ownership (FII 0.01%, DII 0.66%) suggests limited independent scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What looks like a thriving defense growth story on the income statement falls apart on the cash-flow statement. Over 2022-2025 the company reported ₹59 Cr of cumulative net profit yet generated ₹-24 Cr in cumulative operating cash flow and ₹-65 Cr in free cash flow. Growth has been fuelled by a large equity raise in 2024 (equity 25→126 Cr) and working capital absorption, not by owner earnings. In my book, earnings you cannot take to the bank are not earnings.

At ₹1,516 Cr market cap on ₹24 Cr PAT (73x) and 10.9x book, the price embeds many years of flawless execution in a capital-intensive, lumpy-order defense business with no proven moat and no FII/DII validation. Aerospace & Defense can be a fine niche, but I want durable returns on capital, consistent free cash flow, and a fair price — this offers none of the three. I would pass and revisit only if the stock fell 60-70% and cash conversion normalised for at least two years.
